what_the_paper_would_let_us_do: Implement irbesartan from a source with first-order absorption. The only model read in full, Karatza and Karalis 2020 (PMID 32736091, in the archive; two compartments, apparent oral, 32 healthy men, no covariates), absorbs each dose through a delay differential equation, dA0/dt = -ka A0(t - T), with ka T = 0.511 > 1/e, so its input oscillates: 105% of the dose reaches plasma by 6.5 h and 5% flows back to the gut. No nonnegative input the engine can carry gets within 3.5% of that curve (a linear program over any number of pulses), and the best pulse discretisation built (12 default-form oral pulses, as hydrochlorothiazide's Weibull) misses it by 5.8% of the peak (6.4% at a 45 kg woman), ten times the 0.53% standard of docs/adding-a-drug.md, so irbesartan was withheld from PR #818. [decision] for Steven Shafer, raised 2026-11-19: accept Karatza with the 5.8% error stated, or wait for Hedaya and Helmy 2015 (PMID 25545238), whose model the Karatza paper borrowed for its blood-pressure simulations and which is expected to be first order (to be confirmed on the PDF). Karatza's model checked against the Avapro label (not fitted to it): CL/F 13.5 L/h inside the label's 11.8-17.6; Tmax 1.9 h inside 1.5-2 h; terminal half-life 8.2 h against 11-15 h. Karatza's text says nothing is absorbed for the first 1.68 h, but its Table 3 (Tmax 1-2 h at delays to 2.3 h) needs the dose held in the depot before time 0 (Monolix's history convention); that reading reproduces Table 3's Tmax exactly and AUC(0-48) within 0.8%. The Karatza draft (model, test, shared-file patch with the antihypertensive registry record and parameter rows) was not committed; its help-page narrative must be rewritten. Also needed whichever source is used: the drugDefaults row (Antihypertensives), a therapeuticRanges row (none_established), the pregnancy row (not_applicable, ARB fetotoxicity, as valsartan), the antihypertensive registry record and parameters, the three plasma-only rosters, and the Avapro label (archive copy NJ_dailymed-7885b2a8.pdf, md5 12123dca3f7ee8305bd81501a8cc7b64, card papers/digests/NJ_dailymed-7885b2a8.md) in papers/labels with its fdaLabels.csv row.

Liu M, Hu X, Liu J. The effect of hypothermia on isoflurane MAC in children. Anesthesiology 2001;94:429-432. The code says it was read, but its PDF is not in stanpumpRPapers (the archive check in docs/gas-engine-audit/PROMPT.md, section 9), so nobody can re-check the numbers against the source. File the PDF, write its card, and confirm each number below on the PDF. If one differs, change the constant and everything that pins or prints it, in a new pull request. The volatile agents' MAC rests on this paper's regression of isoflurane MAC on temperature in children (37, 34 and 31 C): MAC = 0.0784 T - 1.203. That gives GAS_MAC_ZERO_TEMPERATURE = 1.203/0.0784 = 15.3 C, or 4.6% of the normothermic MAC per degree. The R/physiology.R header says the paper's own text gives 'approximately 5.1%' and a zero at 16.2 C, neither of which follows from its regression. Check all three on the PDF. gasMacTemperatureFactor() applies the regression to sevoflurane, isoflurane and desflurane, to their MAC equivalents, and, since PR #858, to their thresholds (gasThresholdForTemperature()). A copy, PMID_11374601.pdf, is on Dr Shafer's Drive outside the archive, in the folders named CarlisleDownload.

IMPORTANT, and the reason this row was rewritten on 2026-11-25 (CodeRabbit on PR #888): the route is INTRAMUSCULAR only. Every goat had carfentanil 40 ug/kg i.m.; the intravenous, intramuscular and subcutaneous crossover named in the abstract's first sentence is NALTREXONE's, the reversal drug. So this paper gives no intravenous carfentanil arm and no absolute volume or clearance, exactly as Bergh 2019 does not -- the row first claimed the opposite, from reading that sentence and not the rest of the abstract. Read the biphasic parameters and the goats' weights; treat them as evidence about the molecule's shape in a second species, never as a parameter source for people. No intravenous carfentanil study appears in the peer-reviewed literature, but do not write that as an absolute: CodeRabbit pointed at a Feasel 2017 dissertation and a 2018 technical report said to dose four rabbits intravenously, neither of which could be opened (HTTP 403). PubMed's four Feasel carfentanil papers are in vitro or an inhalation biomarker study, so the grey literature is the only open question -- and a dissertation with an intravenous arm would be the first absolute carfentanil disposition in any species. Check it before stating anything absolute in the model header.

Vss 71.5 L is CONFIRMED (Table II), so the unverified search summary was right. V1 is NOT printed, but the 2-compartment model CLOSES: CL, Vss and both half-lives are four non-redundant parameters and V1 = CL/((alpha+beta) - alpha*beta*Vss/CL), linear in 1/V1 and so unique. Table III gives all four PER SUBJECT, so each man's model closes individually and the printed means (means of six separate fits, no subject having that combination) can be replaced by a two-stage refit: simulate the six, take the median at log-spaced times, fit by OLS on the log concentrations. That gives CL 32.28 L/h, V1 16.12, V2 58.50, Vss 74.62, Q 127.4, t1/2 3.55 min and 1.862 h, against the mean set's V1 32.60 and t1/2alpha 11.4 min. Clearance and the volumes are ABSOLUTE, not per kg; Table I gives the six weights (70-79 kg, mean 74.7, ages 24-53, all men), so the cohort anchor is close to the reference man. ORAL: F is per subject and model-independent (22.2 to 136.0%, median 83.7%) and the lag is per subject (0.24-0.50 h), and the input's SHAPE was recovered on 2026-11-27 by digitising Figure 1 and deconvolving subject 1's own closed UDF out of his 7 oral points: the input is ZERO-ORDER, F 105.4%, released over 55 min after a 15.4 min lag (SSlog 0.0592 and AIC -27.40, against a lagged first-order input's 0.3204 and -15.59 at the same parameter count; the first-order input cannot even reach the observed peak, its maximum being 0.935 ug/L against the observed 1.417). So build the oral form with stanpumpR's existing oralZeroOrder = list(duration, lag), not a ka. See the card's open_questions. The card is on PR https://github.com/StevenLShafer/stanpumpR/pull/1004 and the refit's V1 moves 32% with where the simulated grid starts, so treat V1 as determined to about 30% and CL as firm. The six-fold spread in F is real and is NOT a reason to make this IV-only, the IV arm standing on its own. The oral model is settled: see the zero-order result above.

A published relation for the saturated vapour pressure of water against temperature, 28 to 38 C, for the gas engine. Steven L. Shafer decided on 2026-11-27 that water vapour pressure follows body temperature (47 Torr at 37 C exactly), and the relation is still to be chosen and read: the archive holds none (Paper management, 2026-11-28; Peyton 2001 and Curran-Everett 2006 only use the fixed 47 mmHg). Candidates: Buck AL. New equations for computing vapor pressure and enhancement factor. J Appl Meteorol 1981;20:1527-1532 (not in PubMed); the Antoine equation with its source constants; or the IAPWS-95 formulation (Wagner and Pruss, J Phys Chem Ref Data 2002;31:387-535). Any of them is accurate far beyond need over this range (about 28 Torr at 28 C, 35.7 at 32 C, 49.7 at 38 C); the paper is wanted so that the constant in the code is read from its source. It unblocks WATER_VAPOUR_PRESSURE as a function of body$temperature in gasHumidityRatio() and the alveolar partial pressures (GAS_ALVEOLAR_TORR).
